title: Compact diagrams have filtered-colimit-preserving cocone transport
statement:
Use the universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'$, $\kappa$-smallness, $\kappa$-filteredness and $\kappa$-compactness of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category], coherent cocones and colimits of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the join coslice and its projection of [lem-cbc-relative-coslice-left-fibration], and space-valued classification of [lem-coef-space-transport-classification]. Let $\kappa\in\mathcal U$ be an infinite regular cardinal and let $\mathcal E$ be a locally small quasicategory fitting in $\mathcal U'$ and admitting all small $\kappa$-filtered colimits. Let $L$ be a $\kappa$-small simplicial set and $q:L\to\mathcal E$ have $\kappa$-compact values at every vertex. The space-valued functor
$$G_q:\mathcal E\longrightarrow\mathcal S_{\mathcal U'}$$
classified by the left fibration $\mathcal E_{q/}\to\mathcal E$ preserves all small $\kappa$-filtered colimiting coherent cocones. In particular, for every such colimiting cocone $p:I\to\mathcal E$, $p\to\Delta_I c$, the induced coherent cocone $G_qp\to\Delta_I G_q(c)$ is colimiting in spaces, with its actual image cocone maps. The empty simplicial set $L$ is allowed. No colimit of $q$ is assumed to exist.

source.place: Corollary 5.3.4.14, printed p. 401, with Definition 5.3.4.5, printed p. 396 (a compact left fibration is classified by a filtered-colimit-preserving functor). Read online 2026-10-17; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical theorem.

proof.text:
Put $H=\operatorname{Fun}(L,\mathcal E)$ and write $\Delta_L:\mathcal E\to H$ for the constant-diagram functor. The coherent functor calculus makes $H$ a quasicategory. Since $L$ is small and $\mathcal E$ fits in $\mathcal U'$, its internal functor simplicial set fits there too. Apply the space-valued transport classification in a containing universe to obtain the coherent corepresented functor $H(q,-):H\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal U'}$. The join-slice comparison identifies the entire left fibration $\mathcal E_{q/}\to\mathcal E$, naturally over its apex, with the coherent cocone category, whose fiber at $t$ is $\operatorname{Map}_H(q,\Delta_Lt)$. Its apex naturality includes postcomposition: for $v:t\to t'$ the fiber map is $u\mapsto\Delta_L(v)\circ u$, with all higher compatibilities. More explicitly, let $A_q=\{q\}\times_{H,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,H)$, with target projection to $H$. Source-fixed arrow classification makes $A_q\to H$ the left fibration classified by $H(q,-)$. Its pullback $P_q=\mathcal E\times_{H,\Delta_L}A_q$ is exactly the coherent cocone category just used: an $n$-simplex is an apex $t:\Delta^n\to\mathcal E$ and a transformation from the constant $q$-diagram to $\Delta_Lt$. Compatibility of classification with base pullback says that $P_q$ is classified by $H(q,-)\circ\Delta_L$. The join-slice comparison is an equivalence over $\mathcal E$ between $\mathcal E_{q/}$ and this $P_q$, so full coherent classification gives a coherent natural equivalence
$$\alpha:G_q\simeq F_q,\qquad F_q=H(q,-)\circ\Delta_L.$$
This identifies functors and their actual transformations, rather than only unrelated equivalences of vertex spaces.

source.place: Corollary 5.3.4.14, first two sentences and displayed pullback; Proposition 4.2.1.5, Corollaries 4.2.1.7-4.2.1.8 and coherent space-valued classification

proof.text:
Let $I$ be any small $\kappa$-filtered quasicategory, and let $\lambda:p\to\Delta_Ic$ be any colimiting coherent cocone in $\mathcal E$. The pointwise colimit theorem gives $I$-colimits in $H$ and characterizes their cocones by evaluation at every vertex of $L$. At each vertex $l$, evaluation of
$$\Delta_L\lambda:\Delta_Lp\longrightarrow\Delta_I(\Delta_Lc)$$
is exactly $\lambda$, including its legs and higher simplices, because evaluation composed with the constant-diagram functor is the identity. Hence this displayed cocone is colimiting in $H$. Thus the diagonal preserves the tested colimits. No colimit with shape $L$ in $\mathcal E$ has been used.

source.place: Corollary 5.3.4.14, last sentence; Corollary 5.1.2.3, pointwise colimit detection

proof.text:
Apply [lem-coef-pointwise-compact-diagrams] with $K=L$, $\mathcal C=\mathcal E$ and $a=q$. Its cardinal is the given infinite regular $\kappa$; its shape bound and vertex compactness are precisely the hypotheses on $L,q$; its filtered colimits exist by the hypothesis on $\mathcal E$. It says that $q$ is compact in the entire functor category $H$. Unpack the compactness definition and apply it to the specific colimiting $I$-cocone of step 2. It follows that
$$F_qp=\operatorname{Map}_H(q,\Delta_Lp(-))\longrightarrow\Delta_I\operatorname{Map}_H(q,\Delta_Lc)=\Delta_IF_q(c)$$
is colimiting in $\mathcal S_{\mathcal U'}$. Its leg at $i$ is exactly postcomposition by $\Delta_L(\lambda_i)$, since compactness is defined using the image of the given coherent cocone.

source.place: Corollary 5.3.4.14, use of Proposition 5.3.4.13 and Definition 5.3.4.5

proof.text:
Naturality of the equivalence $\alpha$ from step 1 gives, on the whole $I$-cocone, the commutative comparison with components
$$\alpha_c\circ G_q(\lambda_i)\simeq F_q(\lambda_i)\circ\alpha_{p(i)}.$$
The homotopies here are restrictions of one coherent natural equivalence, so retain compatibility on every simplex of $I$. For every test space $Z$, precomposition with the equivalences $\alpha_{p(i)}$ and $\alpha_c$ identifies the map
$$\operatorname{Map}(G_q(c),Z)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(I,\mathcal S_{\mathcal U'})}(G_qp,\Delta_IZ)$$
induced by the actual image cocone with the corresponding map for $F_q$. Precomposition is an equivalence on both sides: a coherent quasi-inverse of $\alpha$ supplies the inverse maps and the two inverse homotopies. The latter map is an equivalence by step 3 and the coherent cocone criterion. The same criterion now makes the actual cocone $G_qp\to\Delta_IG_q(c)$ colimiting. Since $I,p,\lambda$ were arbitrary, this is the required preservation, including the asserted maps.

source.place: Corollary 5.3.4.14, equivalence of the two left-fibration models; coherent cocone universal property

proof.text: All steps allow $L=\varnothing$. In that case $H=\operatorname{Fun}(\varnothing,\mathcal E)$ is the terminal quasicategory by the internal-functor definition, $q$ is its unique object, and $F_q$ is terminal-space-valued. Step 2 still applies by vacuous pointwise detection, and the empty-shape clause of the pointwise-compact-diagram theorem still supplies step 3. Thus no separate assumption on the filtered colimit of terminal spaces is hidden. If $L=\Delta^0$, step 1 reduces to the corepresented functor of its one value and step 3 to its given compactness. No step forms a colimit of $q$, for empty or nonempty $L$.

source.place: Corollary 5.3.4.14 and Proposition 5.3.4.13, empty and singleton indexing shapes
